paragraphs: Mentioned in Ketubot 9:10, where he brought a question before Rabbi Yose [ב)].

notes.text: The ending ב) is unexplained. It may be a note marker or a damaged continuation; no patronymic is supplied.

The later saved named Guggenheimer Ketubot chapter 9, tenth halakhah selection, explicitly has Yudan bar Shikli (שיקלי) bringing a case before Yose. This supplies the occurrence behind the earlier finite spelling nonmatch. Hyman’s paraphrase as a question and הכנים remain unchanged; final ב) remains unresolved and is not made a patronymic or ordinal.

The Hyman scan (vol. II, p. 619) appears to print הכנים in the phrase about bringing a question and shows the final ב) as supplied. That final mark remains unresolved. In Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 9:10, the consulted Guggenheimer and Machon Mamre texts name Yudan bar Shikli (שיקלי), who brings a case before Rabbi Yose about reusing a document. Guggenheimer’s translation gives “from Sicily” and records another interpretation. Neither is needed to explain Hyman’s spelling or final mark.
